items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I wrote a ballet more than ten years ago now... that was commissioned by a company in Columbus, Ohio, and the ballet is called “My Name Is Jasmine But They Call Me Jazz.”

ctx.x: Have these kinds of experiences found their way into inspiration for compositions for you?

Oh yes, of course. I wrote a ballet more than ten years ago now, that was commissioned by a company in Columbus, Ohio, and the ballet is called “My Name Is Jasmine But They Call Me Jazz.” And it was played about five or six times. The ballet had to stay in their control for five years, and we have it now. We haven’t been able to produce it because it’s a big thing to produce a ballet but we have it back now. But I have recorded some of the songs. At that time, when I did it I couldn’t record any of the songs…
There you go. Trying to get something on the page.
